record_verbatim.evidence: MEASURED. The rule as it stands in docs/artifacts/tools/corpus.py: `if d.get("artifact_type") == "requirement" and d.get("engineering_domain") == "safety" and "-FSR-" in _id(key)`, then read diagnostic_coverage, and report if diagnostic_coverage is claimed without diagnostic_coverage_evidence. Corpus-wide scan: diagnostic_coverage is claimed by FSR records and by no SEC record, so 0 requirements are excluded that would otherwise have been reported. The filter is reproducible from the source line alone, and docs/artifacts/tests/rule_scope_probe.py prints it under 'ADJACENT RULE NOTED, NOT CHANGED'.
record_verbatim.impact: Today, no measurable harm, and it is important to say that plainly rather than inflate it. The rule reads the field diagnostic_coverage and the field diagnostic_coverage_evidence. No FB2-SAF-SEC-* record claims diagnostic coverage, so the filter currently excludes nothing that would have been reported: the rule is inert on this corpus, not wrong on it. The harm is prospective and specific. If a future security requirement claims a diagnostic coverage figure - and the security concept does have a diagnostic story, since the requirements mandate a diagnosis entry per rejected frame - the rule would silently decline to check the claim, and the silence would look identical to the silence this finding was raised about in FB2-REV-FND-000039. A check that is inert until the day it is needed, and wrong on that day, is a trap with a long fuse.

record_verbatim.resolution:
RESOLVED. The filter this record identified is gone.

WHAT FIXED IT. The `and "-FSR-" in _id(key)` clause is deleted from the MUT-010 rule in docs/artifacts/tools/corpus.py, so the population is now `artifact_type == requirement and engineering_domain == safety` - the same selection its sibling safety rules use. The finding text was generalised from 'FSR {aid} claims diagnostic coverage' to 'safety requirement {aid} claims diagnostic coverage', because keeping the FSR wording would have been a second and quieter way of encoding the same assumption about the population. Nothing else in the rule changed, and no acceptance gate, scenario, mutation fixture, or coverage-dimension computation was touched; SCN-MUT-010's mutation fixture and oracle manifest were left exactly as they are and still match, because the scenario harness keys on the rule id rather than on the description string.

THE WIDENED RULE WAS MEASURED, AND IT REPORTS NOTHING. On the corpus as it stands: 233 records in the index, 12 of them safety-domain requirements (7 FB2-SAF-FSR-* and 5 FB2-SAF-SEC-*), and 0 of those 12 carries a diagnostic_coverage field at all. Findings reported by diagnostic_coverage_claim_validator: 0. There were no findings to answer by doing the work, and none were re-narrowed away to achieve that.

THAT ZERO IS NOT EVIDENCE THE RULE WORKS, and this is the reason the self-tests below exist. 'Reports nothing on a corpus where nothing is wrong' is not 'would report the defect', which is the entire content of this finding: the harm was always prospective, so a prospective check cannot be validated by a retrospective count. Leaving it at a measured zero would have meant asking the next reader to take the coverage on trust.

PROOF THAT THE RULE IS LIVE, BY COUNTERFACTUAL. Four synthetic records were run through the real _validate_semantic_rules in memory, with nothing on disk changed, and the findings filtered to this rule alone:
  1. FB2-SAF-SEC-999991 claims diagnostic_coverage='99%', evidence field REMOVED
       -> FIRED: high | safety requirement FB2-SAF-SEC-999991 claims diagnostic coverage '99%' without evidence
  2. the same record WITH diagnostic_coverage_evidence present
       -> silent
  3. FB2-SAF-FSR-000003, the record class SCN-MUT-010 exercises
       -> FIRED: high | safety requirement FB2-SAF-FSR-000003 claims diagnostic coverage '99%' without evidence
  4. FB2-SYS-SYR-999988 with engineering_domain=system
       -> silent, as the domain boundary requires
  5. FB2-SAF-SEC-000001 - a real corpus id, in the class the old filter hid
       -> FIRED: high | safety requirement FB2-SAF-SEC-000001 claims diagnostic coverage '90%' without evidence

THE FOUR SELF-TESTS ADDED, following the pattern the MUT-008 fix used, all registered in cmd_selftest:
  diagnostic_coverage rule covers security requirements (widened scope)
  diagnostic_coverage rule still covers FSR requirements (nothing lost)
  diagnostic_coverage rule still respects the safety-domain boundary
  diagnostic_coverage rule silent when evidence is present

THEY ARE NOT VACUOUS EITHER, and that was proved rather than assumed. Re-inserting the old `and "-FSR-" in _id(key)` clause into an in-memory copy of corpus.py and asking the same four questions gives:
  FB2-SAF-SEC-999991  expected_fired=True  got=False  -> the widened-scope test FAILS
  FB2-SAF-FSR-999990  expected_fired=True  got=True   -> passes
  FB2-SAF-FSR-999989  expected_fired=True  got=True   -> passes
  FB2-SYS-SYR-999988  expected_fired=False got=False  -> passes
So a future edit that re-narrows the population fails the suite on this corpus, which is the property the MUT-008 tests were added for and the reason the coverage does not have to be taken on trust.

SUITE STATE AFTER THE CHANGE: selftest 28 -> 32 passing, 0 failing; check PASSED 8/8; validate 0 findings, errors=0. human_approval_status remains pending, production_authorized remains false and product_verification_credit remains false. No human approved this revision, no tool is claimed to be qualified, and no certification, ISO 26262 conformity or ASPICE capability level is claimed or implied.

reverification.evidence: The MUT-010 rule no longer contains an id filter: its population is artifact_type == requirement and engineering_domain == safety, matching the sibling safety rules. The widened rule reports 0 findings on the current corpus because 0 of the 12 safety-domain requirements carries diagnostic_coverage - a measured zero, not a disabled check. The rule is shown live by a counterfactual that fires on a synthetic SEC record with the evidence field removed and on the real id FB2-SAF-SEC-000001, and silent when the evidence is present or the domain is not safety. The four new self-tests are shown non-vacuous: with the old filter restored in memory the widened-scope test fails. selftest 32/32, check 8/8, validate 0 findings errors=0.
reverification.method: Rule source re-read; corpus re-scanned for diagnostic_coverage claims by declared type and domain; counterfactual records run through the real _validate_semantic_rules in memory; non-vacuity proved by re-inserting the old filter in memory; suite re-run via corpus.py selftest, check and validate.

revision_history.description: New record raised by the finding-closure pass. It records a condition that pass discovered while re-deriving the conditions the 38 existing records assert, and that would otherwise have been lost - either because it was a rule defect that no record named, or because closing the record that did name its neighbourhood would have quietly carried it away with it. ACKNOWLEDGED AND NOT FIXED, deliberately, and the reason is scope rather than difficulty. The change to make is a one-clause deletion identical to the one applied in FB2-REV-FND-000039, and it is exactly the kind of change that should not be made in a pass whose authorisation covers one specific rule. Making it here would mean widening a second rule on the strength of a symptom that does not currently manifest, with no measurement showing what the widened rule would report on this corpus. human_approval_status remains pending, production_authorized remains false and product_verification_credit remains false. No human approved this revision, no tool is claimed to be qualified, and no certification, ISO 26262 conformity or ASPICE capability level is claimed or implied.

revision_history.author: verification_engineer
revision_history.description: FILTER REMOVED, WIDENED RULE MEASURED, AND ITS LIVENESS PROVEN BY SELF-TEST AND COUNTERFACTUAL. The '"-FSR-" in id' clause is deleted from the MUT-010 rule in docs/artifacts/tools/corpus.py and the finding text is generalised from 'FSR' to 'safety requirement', so the population is declared type and declared domain like the sibling safety rules. The widened rule was then MEASURED and reports zero findings on the current corpus - 233 records, 12 safety-domain requirements, none carrying diagnostic_coverage - which is a true statement about the corpus and no evidence at all that the rule works. Four self-tests were therefore added, following the pattern the MUT-008 fix used, and a counterfactual confirms the rule fires on an in-memory record with the evidence field removed. Non-vacuity of the self-tests was proved by re-inserting the old filter in memory and observing the security-requirement test fail. No acceptance gate, scenario, mutation fixture or coverage-dimension computation was changed. Disposition moved from 'accepted' to 'resolved' because the condition this record asserts - that the rule carries the filter - no longer holds. human_approval_status remains pending, production_authorized remains false and product_verification_credit remains false. No human approved this revision, no tool is claimed to be qualified, and no certification, ISO 26262 conformity or ASPICE capability level is claimed or implied.

What the validator reads is contract.approval_evidence_block below; it fails if any of its six elements is missing, and the finding names which.
